record.original_question: In infinitary rewriting for orthogonal term-rewriting systems, does the almost-confluence result known for strongly convergent infinite reduction sequences remain valid when infinite reduction sequences are interpreted using the more liberal Cauchy-convergence notion?

evidence.quote: Does “almost-confluence” hold for convergent infinite reduction sequences?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let R be an orthogonal term rewriting system (a first-order TRS whose rewrite rules are left-linear and have no critical pairs). Equip the set of finite and infinite terms over the signature of R with the standard metric d, where d(s,t) = 2^{-n} with n the minimal depth at which s and t differ (and d(s,t)=0 if s=t); under this metric the set of (possibly infinite) terms is a complete metric space.

A transfinite reduction sequence is a sequence of rewrite steps (t_α →_R t_{α+1})_{α<λ} indexed by an ordinal λ. Such a sequence is:
 • Cauchy-convergent (weakly convergent) of length λ to a limit t_λ if, for every limit ordinal μ ≤ λ, the sequence (t_α)_{α<μ} converges to t_μ in the metric d;
 • strongly convergent of length λ to t_λ if it is Cauchy-convergent and, in addition, for every limit ordinal μ ≤ λ the depths of the redexes contracted at steps t_α →_R t_{α+1} tend to infinity as α → μ.

Write s ↠_R^{str} t (resp. s ↠_R^{Cau} t) to mean that there is a strongly convergent (resp. Cauchy-convergent) transfinite reduction sequence from s to t.

It is known that orthogonal TRSs satisfy the following "almost-confluence" property for strongly convergent reductions: whenever s ↠_R^{str} t_1 and s ↠_R^{str} t_2, there exist terms u_1, u_2 and a "hypercollapsing" equivalence ≈ (the equivalence on terms generated by identifying any pair of terms that can be reduced to a common term whose only redex activity sits inside hypercollapsing subterms) such that t_1 ↠_R^{str} u_1, t_2 ↠_R^{str} u_2, and u_1 ≈ u_2.

Question: Does the same almost-confluence property hold for every orthogonal TRS when ↠_R^{str} is replaced everywhere by ↠_R^{Cau}? Equivalently: for every orthogonal TRS R and all terms s, t_1, t_2 with s ↠_R^{Cau} t_1 and s ↠_R^{Cau} t_2, do there exist u_1, u_2 with t_i ↠_R^{Cau} u_i (i=1,2) and u_1 ≈ u_2?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Endrullis, Grabmayer, Hendriks, Klop, and van Oostrom on infinitary rewriting for weakly orthogonal systems and on weak (Cauchy) convergence has clarified large parts of the question: infinitary confluence holds for weakly orthogonal TRSs without collapsing rules, but counterexamples to unique normal forms exist when collapsing rules are present, and structural results relate weakly convergent reductions in orthogonal systems to strongly convergent ones. Thus the question has been substantially resolved in the orthogonal/weakly orthogonal setting, but a single uniform "almost-confluence" statement for arbitrary orthogonal TRSs under Cauchy convergence is not stated as fully settled in a single result.

status_evidence.title: Infinitary Term Rewriting for Weakly Orthogonal Systems: Properties and Counterexamples
status_evidence.snippet: Infinitary confluence, and hence UNfinf, holds for weakly orthogonal TRSs that do not contain collapsing rules; counterexamples with collapsing rules are given; results on weak (Cauchy) convergence in orthogonal systems are established.
status_evidence.claim: Confluence-type questions for orthogonal/weakly orthogonal TRSs under weak (Cauchy) convergence are substantially answered, with positive and negative results depending on collapsing rules.

status_evidence.title: Unique Normal Forms in Infinitary Weakly Orthogonal Rewriting
status_evidence.snippet: Studies unique normal forms in infinitary weakly orthogonal rewriting, including counterexamples involving collapsing rules.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial resolutions of confluence/UN questions for Cauchy-convergent infinitary rewriting in (weakly) orthogonal systems.

status_evidence.title: On Modularity in Infinitary Term Rewriting
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses confluence and almost-confluence properties for infinitary term rewriting, including under different convergence notions.
status_evidence.claim: Relevant follow-up work analyzing confluence properties for infinitary rewriting under Cauchy convergence.
